title: The chat in Claude Code's style: grouped tool steps named by what they did, its reading rhythm, its question cards
request: Owner, with a screenshot of Claude Code's desktop app: make the chat UI like Claude Code, its answering style and its question style.
plan: read how steps, thinking and questions are drawn
group a run of tool calls into one summary line
name each step by what it did
a look in the browser; tests

decisions.decision: a command's step is named by its own description, the raw command kept one click deeper
decisions.why: Claude Code shows what a step did; the command and its output stay for whoever opens it

decisions.decision: a failed step says Failed (Declined when the person said no) in the group's line
decisions.why: a failure must stay visible while the group is closed

findings.defect: the steps line sat at the window's left edge, outside the conversation column
findings.scenario: a session with tool calls, 1440 px: the line at x 158 while the messages started at 270
findings.cause: the new margin shorthand replaced the column's automatic side margins
findings.fix: only top and bottom margins set

findings.defect: the server tests failed with no space left on the device
findings.scenario: the Mac's disk filled while the suite ran
findings.cause: the disk, not the change: the same tests passed once space was free
findings.fix: none in code; rerun after the owner freed space

outcome: The conversation reads like Claude Code's: quiet step lines, clear prose, familiar question cards.
lessons: A margin shorthand on a centred column's child undoes its centring: set only the sides you mean.
